channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Hosting AI Forum in Astana for CIS Countries
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed establishing a permanent mechanism for experience exchange in artificial intelligence at a CIS heads of state meeting. He emphasized the growing role of digitalization and AI in economic competitiveness. Tokayev also suggested holding a specialized CIS AI forum in Astana in the first quarter of next year.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Compensate Drivers for Damage Caused by Substandard Gasoline
item.description: Kazakh drivers can claim compensation for vehicle repairs resulting from poor-quality gasoline, stated Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov. The law on consumer protection mandates sellers to cover damages caused by defective goods. Compensation is due regardless of the seller's or manufacturer's fault, with consumers choosing who pays.

item.title: Tokayev Stresses Preserving Linguistic and Cultural Diversity within CIS
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the importance of preserving the linguistic and cultural diversity of CIS member states. Speaking at the CIS Heads of State Council meeting, he also highlighted the significance of strengthening cultural and humanitarian ties and supporting the Russian language's role in inter-state relations.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Expanding CIS Cooperation in Trade, Industry, Transport, and Energy
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed strengthening cooperation within the CIS in trade, industry, transport, and energy. He also suggested establishing a joint center to combat cybercrime. Mirziyoyev emphasized the importance of economic integration and production cooperation, calling for the full functioning of the Free Trade Zone and mutual recognition of conformity certificates.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Proposes Modernizing the CIS, Citing Outdated 2007 Concept
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed modernizing the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), stating its 2007 development concept is outdated. Speaking at the CIS Heads of State Council meeting, he highlighted the organization's historical mission since the 1991 Almaty Declaration and its role in preventing conflict. Tokayev emphasized the need for direct dialogue amidst global economic and geopolitical uncertainties.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Proposes Reallocating Overpaid Credit Funds to Principal Debt
item.description: Uzbekistan's Antimonopoly Committee has proposed to the Central Bank a revision of the credit payment calculation mechanism to benefit consumers. The committee noted that some banks are not directing overpaid monthly credit installments towards reducing the principal debt, leading to continued interest accrual. This practice violates consumer protection laws.

item.title: Kazakhmys Reports on Nine-Month Performance: Safety Improvements and Production Growth
item.description: Kazakhmys leadership met with work collectives in Balkhash to discuss nine-month results. Key topics included production safety, modernization, and labor conditions. The company reported no fatalities among its workers, a 40% decrease in industrial injuries, and increased drilling volumes. Production of concentrate and cathode copper remains on schedule.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Payment Balance Records Surplus
item.description: Kazakhstan's payment balance has shifted into a surplus, indicating a positive trend in the country's international financial transactions. This development reflects the overall economic health and stability of the nation's financial standing.

item.title: Kazakh President Attends CIS Heads of State Council Meeting
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev attended the CIS Heads of State Council meeting, thanking Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedov for the successful summit and hospitality. Tokayev highlighted the CIS's role in preventing post-Soviet conflicts and its 35th anniversary, referencing the 1991 Almaty Declaration.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Addresses Concerns Over Gasoline Quality
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov responded to a parliamentary inquiry regarding gasoline quality in Kazakhstan. He stated that since the beginning of 2026, 78 control measures, including inspections and test purchases, have been conducted, with 78 gasoline samples collected for laboratory analysis.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Proposes CIS Development Strategy Until 2035
item.description: At the CIS Heads of State Council meeting in Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed developing a CIS Development Strategy until 2035. He emphasized focusing on priorities like economy, energy, infrastructure, high technologies, and human capital to strengthen the CIS's potential and adapt to new geopolitical conditions.

item.title: US Senator Rubio Warns Russia's War Could Spread Beyond Ukraine's Borders
item.description: US Senator Marco Rubio warned that Russia's war in Ukraine is at a stalemate but could escalate into a wider regional conflict if either side pursues dangerous actions. He stated Washington believes in resolving the conflict through negotiations and is ready to mediate, following a deadly attack on buses in Kramatorsk.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Development Strategy for CIS Until 2035
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed the development of a CIS development strategy until 2035. The proposal was made during a meeting of the Council of CIS Heads of State. The strategy aims to foster cooperation and address future challenges within the Commonwealth of Independent States.

item.title: Kazakh President Attends CIS Heads of State Council Meeting in Ashgabat
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev attended the meeting of the Council of CIS Heads of State in Ashgabat. He expressed gratitude to Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdymukhamedov for the summit's organization and hospitality. The meeting focused on regional cooperation and development within the Commonwealth of Independent States.

item.title: Navi Pillay Awarded Nobel Peace Prize for Human Rights and International Law Advocacy
item.description: South African jurist Navi Pillay, former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong work promoting international law and accountability for grave crimes. Her career includes fighting apartheid, prosecuting Rwandan genocide perpetrators, and leading UN human rights initiatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Housing Market Sees Significant Price Increases in September 2026
item.description: In September 2026, new housing in Kazakhstan rose by 10.9% year-on-year, while secondary market apartments increased by 7.9%. Rental prices for furnished housing saw a substantial 16.7% jump. The average price per square meter in new buildings reached 626,252 tenge nationwide.

item.title: Media Expert Proposes Strengthening Trust Among Central Asian Nations
item.description: A media expert suggests developing tourism, volunteerism, and cultural exchanges to enhance mutual trust among Central Asian countries. He emphasized that security in the modern era depends not only on borders and military power but also on water, technology, and information security, requiring regional cooperation.

item.title: Tajikistan and Japan Sign Agreement to Prepare Tajik Youth for Study in Japan
item.description: Tajikistan and Japan have signed a cooperation agreement to create new opportunities for Tajik youth to study in Japan and learn the Japanese language. The agreement was signed by representatives of Tajikistan's Center for International Programs and Japan-China Language Academy. It aims to facilitate Japanese language learning and prepare students.

item.title: Uzbek President Outlines CIS Cooperation Priorities, Emphasizing Trade and Energy
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev highlighted priority areas for cooperation within the CIS, stressing the need to elevate trade and investment partnerships. He also noted the necessity of a long-term forecast for developing the region's energy interdependencies over the next decade.

item.title: Meat Prices Vary Across Kazakhstan's Cities, Statistics Bureau Reports
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Statistics Bureau released average prices for socially significant products as of October 7. Beef with bones averaged 3816 tenge per kilogram, while boneless cost 5027 tenge. Mutton was sold for 4528 tenge and horse meat for 4327 tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan Confirms Five Cases of H1N1 Flu Strain
item.description: Astana and Mangystau region have confirmed the first cases of seasonal flu in Kazakhstan, with five patients testing positive for influenza A(H1N1). The Ministry of Health reported three cases in Astana and two in Mangystau. Over 127,000 cases of ARVI were recorded nationwide in the past week.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Roman Belov Accused of Espionage for Ukraine in Russia; Investigation Concluded
item.description: Kazakhstan national Roman Belov faces espionage and extremism charges in Russia, allegedly for Ukraine. The Orenburg region FSB investigation has concluded. Belov, a tattoo artist from Baikonur, was reportedly lured to Orenburg, beaten, and detained for nearly 11 months in solitary confinement. His case is classified, making verification of charges difficult.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Establishing Fund for Technical Audit of Residential Buildings
item.description: Kazakhstan is exploring the possibility of creating a dedicated fund for the technical audit of residential buildings. The Ministry of Industry and Construction acknowledged a shortage of funds for such audits, which are currently financed by local executive bodies. The proposal aims to address insufficient staffing and resources within local housing inspectorates.

item.title: Tajikistan Proposes Regional Oil Refinery Construction and Green Transition Strategy
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon proposed developing a project for a large regional oil refinery to meet Central Asia's needs. He also suggested a regional green transition strategy focusing on renewable energy and energy efficiency. This initiative follows a similar proposal made in July 2026 and comes amid Tajikistan's request for oil products from Iran.

item.title: Uzbekistan Embassy Warns Travelers to Saudi Arabia of Potential Flight Disruptions
item.description: The Embassy of Uzbekistan has alerted citizens traveling to Saudi Arabia about possible changes to flight schedules and routes due to regional instability. Travelers are advised to avoid areas near the Yemeni border and adhere to safety regulations. The embassy cited the current regional situation as the cause for potential delays or rerouting of flights.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hosts Sultan of Oman, AI Forum, and Jackie Chan Film Shoot
item.description: Kazakhstan's past week featured a state visit from the Sultan of Oman, discussions on expanding energy, transport, and agriculture cooperation. President Tokayev also visited Turkmenistan, proposing increased trade and collaboration in transport, water resources, and AI. Astana hosted a secretariat meeting on world religions, addressing climate change and AI ethics.

item.title: World Bank Raises Uzbekistan's Economic Growth Forecast to 7.9% for 2026
item.description: The World Bank has increased its forecast for Uzbekistan's GDP growth in 2026 from 6.4% to 7.9%, with expectations for 2027 also rising to 7.5%. The bank projects 7.1% growth in 2028. This upward revision is attributed to strong domestic demand, supported by wage increases, employment growth, remittances, and infrastructure investments. Uzbekistan is expected to be the second-fastest growing economy in the region in 2026.

item.title: CIS Supreme Court Heads Discuss Judicial Cooperation and Regional Security
item.description: The Council of Heads of Supreme Courts of CIS member states convened in Minsk. Representatives from Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan participated. The meeting, held during the CIS's anniversary year, focused on harmonizing legislation, protecting citizens' rights, and ensuring security through joint projects and combating crime, terrorism, and extremism.

item.title: BP Returns to Kazakhstan: Contract Expected by Year-End for Ustyurt Block Exploration
item.description: British Petroleum is set to return to Kazakhstan, with a contract anticipated by the end of the year. KazMunayGas confirmed BP's return, with documents for a joint venture and subsoil use contract nearing completion. The focus will be on the Ustyurt block, near the Uzbek border, for geological exploration.

item.title: Tajik President Urges Enhanced CIS Cooperation in Economy, Technology, and Security
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon addressed the CIS summit in Turkmenistan, calling for strengthened cooperation in economy, technology, transport, and security. He highlighted the CIS's role as a platform for political dialogue and development, emphasizing the need to adapt to new realities and leverage digital technologies for future growth.

item.title: CIS Leaders Agree to Strengthen Economic Cooperation and Jointly Combat Security Threats
item.description: CIS heads of state, meeting in Turkmenistan, adopted a joint statement affirming their commitment to developing economic ties, security cooperation, and social protection. The statement highlights the CIS's role as a strategic partnership platform. Key areas for future collaboration include enhancing the free trade zone, promoting industrial cooperation, and strengthening economic security.

item.title: 6,293 corruption crimes detected in nine months in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry reported the detection of 6,293 corruption-related crimes in the first nine months of the year. The most common offenses were embezzlement and misappropriation, followed by bribery and fraud.

item.title: CIS countries set priorities for social development and transport in 2028-2029
item.description: CIS heads of state agreed to declare 2028 the Year of Social Development and Quality of Life and 2029 the Year of Transport Connectivity. Kyrgyzstan proposed the 2028 initiative, focusing on improving citizens' quality of life and social support.

item.title: Tajikistan and Turkmenistan Leaders Emphasize Sustainable Relations
item.description: Leaders of Tajikistan and Turkmenistan highlighted the sustainable development of bilateral relations. During the Avaza Festival, Tajikistan showcased its culture, arts, and national products, underscoring the importance of cultural exchange and economic cooperation between the two nations.

item.title: CIS Summit Held in Turkmenistan's Avaza Tourist Zone
item.description: The summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) heads of state began in Turkmenistan's Avaza tourist zone. The Caspian ecological summit is also scheduled. Presidents Putin and Pezeşkian are attending. Security measures in Türkmenbaşy have reportedly disrupted daily life, limiting transport and internet access.

item.title: Tajik National Survives Omsk Fire with Severe Burns and Fractures
item.description: A 23-year-old Tajik national has been discharged from a Nizhny Novgorod burn center after surviving a fire at a construction site in Omsk. He sustained 50% body burns, four vertebral fractures, and severe respiratory injuries. The fire on August 15 injured 11 workers, resulting in five fatalities.

item.title: Pakistan's Prime Minister Condemns Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description: The Prime Minister of Pakistan has officially condemned the Houthi attacks targeting Saudi Arabia. The statement was made in response to recent escalations in the region. Further details on Pakistan's diplomatic stance were not provided.

item.title: Large Sum of Money Found in Bukhara City Court Chairman's Office; Lawyer Suspected of Attempted Bribery
item.description: Uzbekistan's Supreme Judicial Council commented on the discovery of a large amount of foreign currency in the office of the Bukhara city court chairman while a local lawyer was present. The lawyer is suspected of attempting to bribe officials. An investigation is ongoing.

item.title: UzPost Plans to Attract 360 Billion Soums in Loans, State Assets Agency Reports
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Assets Management Agency plans to attract 360 billion soums in loans for UzPost. A final decision on privatization has not been made. The agency aims to introduce modern corporate governance mechanisms, drawing on expertise from foreign financial institutions, to compete with companies like Uzum and Wildberries.

item.title: Ukraine National Detained in Kazakhstan Released After Russia's Extradition Request
item.description: A Ukrainian national, Lyubov Rozhanskaya, detained in Astana at Russia's request, has left Kazakhstan and is in the EU. Russia accused her of child abduction and sought extradition via the CSTO. A Kazakh court did not impose pre-trial detention, leading to her release. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry and Ombudsman advocated for her release.
